title: A counterexample to Abel-type asymptotics for scaled Volterra equations
summary: We consider scaled Volterra equations of the form $f_n + n k*f_n = g$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, where $g$ is given and $f_n$ is sought. We show that global two-sided Abel-type bounds on a positive kernel $k$ do not force the solutions $f_n$ to converge to zero as $n \to +\infty$. More precisely, we construct a continuous strictly positive kernel globally comparable with the Abel kernel $x^{-1/2}$, and a continuous strictly positive $g$, for which a subsequence of $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ diverges to $+\infty$ at some point $x_0 > 0$.
